claim: A LAG does not make connectivity to AWS more resilient: with more than one link and minimum links set to one it protects against a single link failure, but not against a single device failure or device maintenance at AWS where the LAG terminates.
question: Does a link aggregation group (LAG) make a Direct Connect connection more resilient?

values.display: a LAG doesn't make your connectivity to AWS more resilient
values.spoken: a LAG protects from a link failure, not from a device failure

qualifiers.condition: more than one link in the LAG and minimum links set to one protects against single link failure only

evidence.quote: No, a LAG doesn't make your connectivity to AWS more resilient. If you have more than one link in your LAG, and if your minimum links are set to one, your LAG will let you protect against single link failure. However, it will not protect against a single device failure or device maintenance at AWS where your LAG is terminating.

note: FAQ question: 'Does having a link aggregation group (LAG) make my connection more resilient?' (item 21).

claim: To achieve high availability connectivity to AWS, AWS recommends making connections at multiple AWS Direct Connect locations.

values.spoken: connect at more than one Direct Connect location

evidence.quote: To achieve high availability connectivity to AWS, we recommend making connections at multiple AWS Direct Connect locations.

note: FAQ question: 'Does having a link aggregation group (LAG) make my connection more resilient?' (item 21).

claim: AWS recommends a second connection for redundancy; when you request multiple ports at the same Direct Connect location, they are provisioned on redundant AWS equipment.
question: How do you order Direct Connect connections for high availability, and where are multiple ports at one location placed?

values.display: provisioned on redundant AWS equipment
values.spoken: multiple ports at one location land on redundant equipment

qualifiers.condition: multiple ports requested at the same location

evidence.quote: We recommend establishing a second connection for redundancy. When you request multiple ports at the same AWS Direct Connect location, they will be provisioned on redundant AWS equipment.

note: FAQ question: 'How do I order connections to AWS Direct Connect for high availability?' (item 22).

claim: With a backup IPsec VPN configured, all VPC traffic fails over to the VPN automatically and traffic to public resources such as Amazon S3 goes over the internet; with no backup Direct Connect link or VPN, VPC traffic is dropped when the connection fails.
question: What happens to VPC traffic when a Direct Connect connection fails, with and without a backup VPN?

values.display: all VPC traffic will failover to the VPN connection automatically
values.spoken: VPC traffic fails over to the VPN automatically

values.display: Amazon VPC traffic will be dropped in the event of a failure

qualifiers.condition: backup IPsec VPN configured versus no backup Direct Connect link or IPsec VPN link

evidence.quote: If you have configured a backup IPsec VPN connection instead, all VPC traffic will failover to the VPN connection automatically. Traffic to/from public resources, such as Amazon S3, will be routed over the internet. If you do not have a backup AWS Direct Connect link or an IPsec VPN link, then Amazon VPC traffic will be dropped in the event of a failure. Traffic to/from public resources will be routed over the internet.

note: FAQ question: 'How do I order connections to AWS Direct Connect for high availability?' (item 22).

values.spoken: no VPN backup for a Local Zone; use two Direct Connect connections

note: FAQ question: 'Can I use AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a backup for my AWS Direct Connect link to an AWS Local Zone?' (item 49).

values.spoken: two links for 100 or 400 gigabit ports

values.spoken: LAG links are active/active

claim: Minimum links is a LACP setting for the minimum number of links that must be active for the LAG bundle to be active and pass traffic; for example, with four ports and minimum links set to three, a bundle with only two active ports is not active.
question: What does minimum links mean for a LAG?

values.display: the minimum number of links that must be active in a bundle
values.spoken: the bundle only works if enough links are active

evidence.quote: Minimum links is a feature in LACP where you can set the minimum number of links that must be active in a bundle for that bundle to be active and pass traffic. If, for example, you have four ports, your minimum links is set to three, and you only have two active ports, your bundle will not be active.

note: FAQ question: 'What does minimum links mean, and why do I have a check box for it when I order my bundle?' (item 73).

claim: AWS Direct Connect has two separate charges, port hours and data transfer; pricing is per port-hour consumed for each port type, partial port hours are billed as full hours, and the account that owns the port is charged the port-hour charges.

values.spoken: port hours and data transfer

evidence.quote: AWS Direct Connect has two separate charges: port hours and data transfer. Pricing is per port-hour consumed for each port type. Partial port hours consumed are billed as full hours. The account that owns the port will be charged the port hour charges.
